mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate indicates a robust economy, leading to higher consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 1.5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and subsequently driving down the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of rising unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates a strong supply chain, leading to increased economic growth and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong industrial production growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between GDP growth rate and consumer spending indicates a robust economy, leading to higher S&P 500 index returns over the next 20 trading days when both are increasing.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when both GDP growth rate and consumer spending are increasing (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between the federal funds rate and inflation rate indicates a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased S&P 500 index returns over the next 5 trading days when the federal funds rate is rising and inflation is high.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in tightening periods with high inflation are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of falling unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between housing starts and consumer spending indicates a robust economy, leading to higher S&P 500 index returns over the next 20 trading days when both are increasing.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when both housing starts and consumer spending are increasing (t-test p > 0.05).
